keyVerseText: Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign; Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel . shall call: or, thou, O virgin, shalt call
rootMeaning: The name עִמָּנוּאֵל (ʻImmânûwʼêl) is derived from the Hebrew root עִם (ʻim), meaning 'with,' combined with a pronominal suffix meaning 'us,' and the word אֵל (El), meaning 'God.' Literally, it means 'with us is God' or 'God with us.' This etymology emphasizes the intimate presence of God alongside His people, highlighting not just a general accompaniment but a divine nearness and solidarity that transcends mere physical proximity.
usageInScripture: The word עִמָּנוּאֵל appears twice in Scripture and is primarily used as a proper name, most notably in Isaiah 7:14 where it is translated as 'O Immanuel.' This name functions both as a symbolic and prophetic title, particularly identifying the Messiah, the Christ, who is foretold to be 'God with us.' The consistent translation and usage underscore the name's role as a declaration of divine presence and assurance to God's people.
theologicalSignificance: The name עִמָּנוּאֵל carries profound theological weight because it encapsulates the mystery of the Incarnation—God Himself coming to dwell among humanity. As a prophetic name of the Messiah, it assures believers that God is not distant or detached but actively present in their lives. This presence brings comfort, deliverance, and confidence, affirming that God’s people are never abandoned. Understanding this name enriches faith by revealing the personal and relational nature of God’s intervention through Christ.
keyVerseReflection: Isaiah 7:14 declares, 'Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign; Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel.' Here, the name עִמָּנוּאֵל profoundly anchors the promise of God's direct involvement with His people. It signals not only a miraculous birth but also the assurance that God is present with His people in their trials, embodying hope and divine companionship through the Messiah.
